fixes.explanation: That's a reasonable thing to think about, friend, but the oath isn't about land. The LORD swears that never again will any man of Judah in Egypt "…invoke My name or say, ‘As surely as the Lord GOD lives.’" The oath is about their words, not their property.

Walls get blamed for a lot, friend. I once blamed my stamp for a crooked cookie when it was my own mustache slipping. Nobody in this passage mentions the walls, though. The LORD points to the evil they did and the other gods they served.

I can see why you'd think so, friend. But the LORD says these were gods "…that neither they nor you nor your fathers ever knew." That's the opposite of old family favorites. These gods were strangers to them all.

That's the one, baker. The LORD says, "They will all fall by the sword or be consumed by famine." Then He says it again for emphasis: "From the least to the greatest, they will die by sword or famine…" That sentence reaches from the least to the greatest.
Not this time, baker. The LORD says, "I will punish those who live in the land of Egypt, just as I punished Jerusalem…" So Egypt is not a safe spot. The answer is True.
That's what they say, baker. The assembly tells Jeremiah, the prophet, "…we will not listen to you!" It's a no from a great assembly.

Let's look at it again, baker. The people really do say it. They say that since they stopped, "…we have lacked everything and have been perishing by sword and famine." It's their own version of events, and it's what the question was asking about.
That's the one, baker. The LORD says the whole remnant "…will know whose word will stand, Mine or theirs!" The question on the table was whose word holds up. They'll find out.
I can see the pull of it, baker, since cities come up a lot in this chapter. But the LORD says they "…will know whose word will stand, Mine or theirs!" It's about words, not cities.

Yes, baker. The LORD says, "…I will deliver Pharaoh Hophra king of Egypt into the hands of his enemies who seek his life…" Pharaoh Hophra is the king of the very land these people went to. That land has a king with trouble of his own.
